altitude.quote: at an altitude of approximately 1400 m above sea level

coordinates.note: The Central Laser Facility at the centre of the Telescope Array surface detector, the array's own reference point (the station table's origin). Replaces a 0.1°-rounded point with 6 km precision. Kept as an approximate campus point because the only fetched source is a collaboration preprint (A17).
coordinates.quote: inside a circle of radius 25 km, centered at the CLF (39.296918 N Lat, 112.908733 W Long).

name: Telescope Array central site, near Delta, Utah
notes: No per-station or per-fluorescence-site coordinates were recorded in this wave; only this single approximate campus point.

summary.plain: The high desert near Delta, Utah, where the Telescope Array's hundreds of ground detectors and telescope stations are spread out to catch ultra-high-energy cosmic rays.
summary.technical: Approximate central/campus point (Delta, Utah, Millard County) for the Telescope Array observatory, at about 1400 m altitude; the actual detector footprint (507 scintillation counters over ~700 km^2, extended to ~3000 km^2 by TAx4, plus fluorescence stations at Middle Drum, Long Ridge and Black Rock Mesa) is spread around this point.
